title: Doenjang Jjigae: Korean Soybean Paste Stew with Tofu, Courgette and Potato
summary: A quick anchovy and kelp stock seasoned with doenjang, simmered with potato, courgette, shiitake and tofu, and finished with fresh chillies.
equipment: medium saucepan or Korean earthenware pot (about 2 litres)

ingredients.item: piece dried kelp (dasima or kombu), about 10 cm square

ingredients.note: check the label: some contain wheat

ingredients.item: small potato, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
small courgette, quartered lengthways and cut into 1.5 cm chunks
fresh shiitake mushrooms, stems removed, caps cut into thick strips
firm tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes

steps.title: Make a quick stock
steps.text: Put the water, kelp and anchovies in the pan and bring slowly to a simmer. Cook gently for 10 min, then lift out the kelp. The anchovies dissolve and give the stock a savoury backbone.

steps.title: Dissolve the paste
steps.text: Hold the small sieve in the stock and press the doenjang through with the back of a spoon. Sieving stops the thick paste from forming lumps.

steps.title: Start the potato
steps.text: Add the potato and onion and simmer for 6 min. Potato goes in first because it takes longest to soften.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Stir in the courgette and mushrooms and simmer for 5 min, until a knife slides easily into the potato.

steps.title: Add the tofu
steps.text: Slide in the tofu and garlic and simmer for 3 min, stirring gently so the cubes hold their shape.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Scatter in the chillies and spring onion, cook for 1 min more and taste. Serve bubbling hot, with rice.

tips: A common mistake is adding all the doenjang in one lump; press it through a sieve so it melts evenly.
Doenjang strengths vary; start with 2 tbsp and add more after tasting if you like it stronger.
Use a lighter hand with the green chilli for a milder stew.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat until piping hot (74 °C). The tofu and potato soften on standing; freezing is not recommended. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
